items.informal_name: Absolute Value Inequality for Elements in an Unordered Interval
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup α] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] {a b c : α},
  c ∈ Set.uIcc a b → |c - a| ≤ |b - a|
items.informal_description: For any elements $a, b, c$ in a linearly ordered additive commutative group, if $c$ belongs to the unordered closed interval $[a, b]$, then the absolute value of $c - a$ is less than or equal to the absolute value of $b - a$, i.e., $|c - a| \leq |b - a|$.

items.informal_name: Absolute Value Inequality for Points in an Unordered Interval
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup α] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] {a b c : α},
  c ∈ Set.uIcc a b → |b - c| ≤ |b - a|
items.informal_description: For any elements $a, b$ in a linearly ordered additive commutative group, if $c$ lies in the unordered closed interval $[a, b]$, then $|b - c| \leq |b - a|$. The absolute value is defined as the supremum of an element and its additive inverse, and the interval contains all elements between the infimum and supremum of $a$ and $b$.

items.informal_name: Absolute Difference Inequality for Nested Intervals
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup α] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] {a b c d : α},
  Set.uIcc c d ⊆ Set.uIcc a b → |d - c| ≤ |b - a|
items.informal_description: If the unordered closed interval $[c, d]$ is a subset of the unordered closed interval $[a, b]$, then the absolute value of the difference $d - c$ is less than or equal to the absolute value of the difference $b - a$, i.e., $|d - c| \leq |b - a|$.

items.informal_name: Absolute Difference Inequality in an Interval
items.type:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup G] [inst_1 : LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G] {a b lb ub : G},
  lb ≤ a → a ≤ ub → lb ≤ b → b ≤ ub → |a - b| ≤ ub - lb
items.informal_description: For any elements $a$ and $b$ in an additive commutative group $G$ equipped with a linear order and ordered add monoid structure, if $lb \leq a \leq ub$ and $lb \leq b \leq ub$, then the absolute value of their difference satisfies $|a - b| \leq ub - lb$.

items.informal_name: Diameter of Closed Interval [a, b] Equals b - a
items.type: ∀ {a b : ℝ}, a ≤ b → Metric.diam (Set.Icc a b) = b - a
items.informal_description: For real numbers $a$ and $b$ with $a \leq b$, the diameter of the closed interval $[a, b]$ is equal to $b - a$, i.e., $\operatorname{diam}([a, b]) = b - a$.

items.informal_name: Diameter of Left-Closed Right-Open Interval in Real Numbers
items.type: ∀ {a b : ℝ}, a ≤ b → Metric.diam (Set.Ico a b) = b - a
items.informal_description: For real numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfying $a \leq b$, the diameter of the left-closed right-open interval $[a, b)$ is equal to $b - a$. This follows from the definition of diameter as the supremum of pairwise distances in the metric space structure on $\mathbb{R}$, where distances are given by absolute differences.
